entries.title: One row per session with what the reviewers said
entries.summary: In the Report Builder, add a scorecard question to a Sessions report and it arrives summarised for each session: Yes/No and other choices as counts (**Yes: 2 / No: 1**), scales and scores as an average, comments with the reviewer's initials. Speakers and tags can still be pivoted, so the report stays one row per session. **How to show this** switches a question to **One row per review**, and **Reviews pivot** gives one block of columns per reviewer. In SbQL: `COUNT_BY_VALUE` and `LIST_WITH_REVIEWER`, and review aggregates next to ordinary columns summarise each session.

where.path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Reviews

entries.use_case: A conference committee wants one spreadsheet row per submission with the session details, the speakers, the average score, how many reviewers called it a sales pitch and every reviewer's final comment. CS built this for AVIXA with SQL; it is now a few clicks in the Report Builder.

cs_action.note: No setup. Reports that already exist are unchanged.

internal.gotchas: Abstentions are left out of the counts and comments. On a blind Review plan comments are listed without initials. The summaries count each review once even when a session has several speakers or tags.
internal.staff_path: Reporting → Reports → Report Builder (Sessions) → search a question → click it
internal.talk_track: Pick your scorecard questions by name and get one row per session, with the Yes/No counts and comments already summarised.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a review summary sheet, Yes/No tallies per submission, or comments from every reviewer next to the session details.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Plan 2.0 Review plans, especially CFP programs that hand a summary sheet to a program committee.
